A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ViewMask-1-to-3. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and added analyses.

before.justification: v2 reports original GSO and 3D-FUTURE evaluations, mask-schedule experiments, GenEval results and qualitative task demonstrations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and additionally reports view-count scalability, inference efficiency and tokenizer comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains MAGVIT-v2 tokenization, the sequence templates, random masking, three-stage training, masked-token loss and predict-remask inference. The higher-view experiments vary sequence-length configurations and fine-tuning budgets without specifying a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Appendix C expands evaluation to standalone visual-tokenizer reconstruction on TokBench. Appendix B.2 additionally reports using BLIP-60K image-caption data before GenEval evaluation. The original multi-view datasets and the previously demonstrated T2I, MMU and rotation tasks remain.

E2.justification: Table 7 introduces a broad component-level comparison of the selected tokenizer with alternatives including TiTok, FlexTok, UniTok and continuous autoencoders. SD3.5-L is added to the GenEval comparison. TRELLIS is removed from Table 1, while remaining in Table 2 and qualitative comparisons.

E3.justification: New protocols include six- and eight-view GSO configurations with 9k-step adaptation, latency-per-view and memory profiling, and tokenizer reconstruction evaluation including rFID. The original camera/rendering rules and 20-step inference setting remain. The newly stated GenEval training details do not establish that its experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the unchanged mask-schedule ablation, v3 tests scaling to more views and beyond the original training token budget, examines computational efficiency, and compares tokenizer reconstruction tradeoffs. These address additional questions about scalability, practical costs and component choice.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. The added tables continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes all six ViewMask image-quality scores: for example, GSO PSNR changes from 20.3868 to 20.6112 and 3D-FUTURE PSNR from 19.8186 to 19.9953. Its reported average rank changes from 1.7 to 1.3, with a reduced comparator set. New scalability, efficiency, tokenizer and SD3.5-L result entries substantially expand the evidence. Tables 2 and 3 and ViewMask's GenEval score of 0.72 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–3 and the mathematical formulation are unchanged. The new tokenizer and diffusion discussions introduce no formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about discrete multi-view generation, consistency without specialized geometry and benchmark performance retain their meaning. The abstract foregrounds MMU/T2I extensions already claimed in v2 and specifies continuous diffusion models as the reference for the retained 10.6% IoU claim.

C2.justification: v3 explains that additional viewpoints can be easier because they are closer to the input view, discusses efficiency versus memory and task versatility, and acknowledges finite-codebook errors in high-frequency details. Appendix C argues that discretization is not the dominant bottleneck. Existing viewpoint-diversity and lighting limitations remain.

D1.justification: New disclosures include model size, inference memory, 9k-step higher-view adaptation, 16× tokenizer downsampling and 5k BLIP-60K training steps before GenEval. The 24 H200 GPUs, batch size 384, learning rate, Zero-2 strategy and 20 sampling steps were already documented in v2; their main-text placement is a move.

R1.justification: The introduction expands its unified understanding/generation context with additional citations, while Appendix C adds TokBench and Lumina-mGPT 2.0 positioning. The GSO citation is corrected and the Objaverse-XL reference disappears. Most related-work arguments remain unchanged; publication-metadata updates do not constitute new cited work.

P1.justification: v3 revises the introductory framing, adds 'Discrete' to the title, corrects the repeated Stage-2 introductory description and moves experimental settings into Section 4. It inserts scalability and efficiency subsections, Appendix C and an impact statement, while retaining most existing prose and section order.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a different conference layout with revised title/author placement, running headers, citation styling and text/float flow. It adds three substantial tables for scalability, efficiency and tokenizers and expands the GenEval table. All eight existing figures retain their content despite relocation and resizing.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses v2's lack of scalability and resource analysis through Tables 4–5 and improves transparency about training behind the unchanged GenEval score. These help assess practical applicability. The gains remain limited by sparse profiling details and conflicting tokenizer identification: Table 7 lists MAGVIT-v2 with 8,192 codes, whereas Section 3.2 specifies 2^18.
